context.body: Now these are those who came to David to Ziklag while he was a fugitive from Saul the son of Kish. They were among the mighty men, his helpers in war.

observations.body: Benjaminites, Gadites, and others come to David; he tests their intent, the spirit clothes Amasai, and help continues until the company resembles God’s army.
observations.label: Warriors join David while Saul still excludes him: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, Benjaminite archers, Gadites, Amasai, Manassites, and Saul, Ziklag, the stronghold, wilderness, and Jordan crossing, coming, testing loyalty, speaking by the spirit, appointing, helping, and growing visible within David's story or later memory.

payload.posture: Read 1 Chronicles 12:1–22 as its own succession, retelling, and temple preparation David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places Chronicles fills the fugitive years with a widening coalition inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
